- Keep the name stable: readers and links find the topic by it.
- Pick a name `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs` does not already list: no Core topic, and no section such as `tokens` or `layout`. To take over or add to a Core topic, see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/docs/extend-or-replace`.

##### Write the sections

A topic is a plain object with `type: 'generic'`, a `name`, a `title`, a one-sentence `description`, and `sections`. Each section has a `title` and a list of `content` blocks.

docs/deploying.doc.mjs:
```javascript
/** @type {import('@astryxdesign/cli/authoring').ReferenceDoc} */
export default {
  type: 'generic',
  name: 'deploying',
  title: 'Deploying',
  description: 'Ship an app built with Acme widgets.',
  sections: [{
    id: 'build-before-you-ship',
    title: 'Build before you ship',
    content: [
      {type: 'prose', text: 'Build the app, then upload the `dist` folder.'},
      {type: 'code', lang: 'bash', code: '{@pm run build}'},
      {type: 'list', style: 'unordered', items: ['Keep `dist` out of git.']},
      {type: 'table', headers: ['Variable', 'Value'], rows: [['`NODE_ENV`', '`production`']]},
    ],
  }],
};
```

The sample sets a section `id`, so `package.json` needs the CLI peer `"@astryxdesign/cli": ">=0.6.4"`. Published 0.6.3 and earlier reject `id` and hide every doc topic your package ships, and `integration verify` fails without that peer; see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/versioning`.

- Replace the `Overview` placeholder `integration add` writes.
- Every field is in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring reference-doc`.

##### Write commands for every reader

Write an Astryx command as `{@command doctor}` and a package-manager step as `{@pm install @acme/widgets}`, never with a runner such as npx or pnpm exec, or a package manager's own command, in front. The CLI shows each one with the command the reader runs: `pnpm exec astryx doctor` or `yarn astryx doctor`, `pnpm add @acme/widgets` or `npm install @acme/widgets`, or the `cliCommand` an integration sets. `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/docs/doc-syntax` lists every token. A command written bare, the word astryx and a command, is shown the same way. `doctor integration validate` (and so `integration check`) names each command written another way, with the token that replaces it; `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/docs/doc-syntax` lists what it checks. An install step, which runs before the CLI is installed, is `{@pm dlx @astryxdesign/cli init}`.

docs/deploying.doc.mjs:
```javascript
{type: 'prose', text: 'Check the app with {@command doctor} before you ship.'},
{type: 'code', lang: 'bash', code: '{@command doctor}'},
```

Read in an app whose integration sets cliCommand: 'acme astryx':
```text
Check the app with `acme astryx doctor` before you ship.

```bash
acme astryx doctor
```
```

- The CLI prefixes an inline code span that starts with the word astryx, a command at the start of a line, or after `&&`, `||`, `;` or `|`, in a `bash`, `sh`, `shell`, `zsh`, `console`, `text` or `markdown` code block or one with no language, and a table cell that holds only a command.
- Code in other languages, such as a `js` example, and the word astryx in plain prose stay as written.
- `--json` returns the doc as written, so a reader that shows it prefixes the commands itself.

##### Pick the doc kind

Every doc is a `.doc.mjs` file whose `type` says what it describes. `integration add` writes the right `type` and file for each kind.

You document                | `type`                | File that `integration add` writes                             
--------------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------
A guide or topic            | `'generic'`           | `docs/deploying.doc.mjs`                                       
Your package's docs section | `'namespace'`         | `docs/acme.doc.mjs`                                            
A component                 | `'component'`         | `components/AcmeCarousel.doc.mjs`, beside `AcmeCarousel.tsx`   
A template                  | `'page'` or `'block'` | `templates/acme-dashboard.doc.mjs`, beside `acme-dashboard.tsx`
A theme                     | `'theme'`             | `themes/ocean/oceanTheme.doc.mjs`, beside `oceanTheme.ts`      

Only guides, topics, and your docs section go in the `docs` root. The others have their own guides: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/components`, `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/templates`, and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/themes`.

##### Keep topics in the docs root

The `docs` field in `astryx.integration.mjs` names the folder that holds your topics. The CLI reads every `.doc.mjs` file under it, in subfolders too.

astryx.integration.mjs:
```javascript
export default {
  docs: './docs'
};
```

- Readers open a topic by its `name`, not its file name. Name the file after the doc, `<name>.doc.mjs`, so each one is easy to find.
- A topic with no `placement` is a flat topic: the docs list shows it under Topics, and readers open it by its name.
- For a section of your own in the docs tree, see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/docs/sections-and-placement`.

##### In global mode

In global mode: when users install your package for their computer, beside the global CLI, your doc topics show up in folders outside any project; inside a project, only if the project installs your package. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/global-integrations`.

#### Doc syntax (building-blocks/docs/doc-syntax)

The tokens a doc writes for links, Astryx commands and package-manager steps, which the CLI shows each reader in their own package manager.

##### The tokens

A doc never names a package manager or a runner: readers use npm, pnpm, Yarn or Bun, and run the CLI through their own. Write a token instead, and the CLI shows each reader the command they run. Tokens work in prose, list items, table cells and code blocks.

Write                                 | For                                    | A pnpm reader sees                       
------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -----------------------------------------
`{@link generic:deploying}`           | another doc                            | the command that opens that doc          
`{@command docs theme}`               | an Astryx command                      | `pnpm exec astryx docs theme`            
`{@pm install @acme/widgets --dev}`   | a package-manager step                 | `pnpm add -D @acme/widgets`              
`{@pm-only npm "why" pkg set name=x}` | a step only one package manager can do | `npm pkg set name=x` (only with npm: why)
`{@@pm install x}`                    | a token shown as written               | `{@pm install x}`                        

In prose a token prints as a code span; in a code span or code block it prints as the command alone. `--json` carries the same commands, a `{@command}` token as the bare command that starts with astryx, which a reader that shows the doc prefixes itself.

##### Package-manager steps

A `{@pm}` token is a verb, its names, and the flags it takes. Each row below runs the same way in every package manager; the CLI writes the reader's own.

Token                              | npm                          | pnpm                              | Yarn                                                  | Bun                          
---------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | -----------------------------
`{@pm install}`                    | `npm install`                | `pnpm install`                    | `yarn install`                                        | `bun install`                
`{@pm install x}`                  | `npm install x`              | `pnpm add x`                      | `yarn add x`                                          | `bun add x`                  
`{@pm install x --dev}`            | `npm install -D x`           | `pnpm add -D x`                   | `yarn add -D x`                                       | `bun add -d x`               
`{@pm install x --global}`         | `npm install -g x`           | `pnpm add -g x`                   | `yarn global add x` (Yarn 1); npm on Yarn 2 and newer | `bun add -g x`               
`{@pm remove x}`                   | `npm uninstall x`            | `pnpm remove x`                   | `yarn remove x`                                       | `bun remove x`               
`{@pm update x --latest}`          | `npm install x@latest`       | `pnpm update --latest x`          | `yarn up x`                                           | `bun update --latest x`      
`{@pm run build --watch}`          | `npm run build -- --watch`   | `pnpm run build --watch`          | `yarn run build --watch`                              | `bun run build --watch`      
`{@pm exec tsc}`                   | `npx tsc`                    | `pnpm exec tsc`                   | `yarn run tsc`                                        | `bunx tsc`                   
`{@pm dlx @astryxdesign/cli init}` | `npx @astryxdesign/cli init` | `pnpm dlx @astryxdesign/cli init` | `yarn dlx …` (`npx` on Yarn 1)                        | `bunx @astryxdesign/cli init`
`{@pm create vite}`                | `npm create vite`            | `pnpm create vite`                | `yarn create vite`                                    | `bun create vite`            

- Flags: `--dev` and `--exact` with `install`, `--global` with `install` and `remove`, `--latest` with `update`. `--exact` takes one version, never a range: only npm pins a range.
- Everything after the name of a script (`run`), a binary (`exec`) or a package (`dlx`, `create`) is passed to it as written.
- `{@pm install x --global}` on pnpm needs `pnpm setup` once per computer.

##### A step only one package manager can do

Some commands exist in one package manager only, such as `npm pkg set` or `pnpm setup`. Write `{@pm-only <manager> "<reason>" <command>}`: the manager is one of npm, pnpm, yarn, yarn-classic or bun, and the reason, in double quotes, is shown to readers beside the command. Use it only when no `{@pm}` step does the same: doctor names a one-manager step that every package manager can run, with the `{@pm}` token to write.

##### What doctor checks

`doctor integration validate`, and so `integration check`, lists each of these as a note with its file, line and the token to write. A note fails nothing today; the next minor release turns them into warnings, so `integration check --strict --next` fails on them now. Run it to fix them ahead.

Note                      | When                                                                                  
------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`package_manager_command` | a code span or shell line written for one package manager, such as `npm install -D x` 
`runner_command`          | an Astryx command written with a runner, such as `pnpm exec astryx docs`              
`plain_command`           | an Astryx command written bare, where `{@command docs}` checks that the command exists
`doc_token`               | a token that does not parse, or a name that is not a doc token                        

In global mode: outside a project, a `{@command}` token prints the way your global install prints every command, and a `{@pm}` step prints for npm unless the CLI detects another package manager. In a project, the project's own runner and package manager decide. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global`.

#### Sections and placement (building-blocks/docs/sections-and-placement)

Give your package its own docs section and place guides in it.

##### Add a docs section

Give your package its own section in the docs tree with `integration add doc <name> --parent <section>`. The first run also writes the section's namespace doc.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration add doc deploying --parent acme
# Open your section
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs acme
```

docs/acme.doc.mjs:
```javascript
/** @type {import('@astryxdesign/cli/authoring').NamespaceDoc} */
export default {
  type: 'namespace',
  name: 'acme',
  title: 'Acme',
  summary: 'Guides for Acme.',
  slots: {
    guides: {title: 'Guides', accepts: {kinds: ['generic']}},
  },
};
```

- Edit its `title` and `summary`: readers see them in the docs list and at the top of your section.
- The guide, `docs/deploying.doc.mjs`, gets `placement: {parent: 'namespace:acme', slot: 'guides'}`. Later runs with `--parent acme` reuse the namespace doc.
- `package.json` gets the optional peer `"@astryxdesign/cli": ">=0.6.4"`, because an older CLI does not read sections; see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/versioning`.

##### Place a doc

A guide names its one home with `placement`: a namespace of your package, a slot in it, and an `order`. Its route is the section name, then the guide name.

```javascript
placement: {parent: 'namespace:acme', slot: 'guides', order: 10}, // route: acme/deploying
```

- Every field is in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring authored-doc-graph-fields`.
- A placed guide opens only by its route, `acme/deploying`. Its bare name no longer opens it.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs acme/deploying
```

##### Fix a failed placement

A failed `placement` hides the doc: it gets no route and does not show in the docs list. `doctor integration docs` fails with `invalid_doc_graph` and names what to fix.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration docs
```

```text
severity: [fail]
code:     invalid_doc_graph
message:  @acme/astryx-widgets/deploying.doc.mjs: placement.parent "namespace:cli" names no namespace; @acme/astryx-widgets declares "acme".
```

- A `parent` your package does not ship, such as `namespace:cli`, "names no namespace".
- A `slot` the namespace does not declare "is not a slot of namespace"; the message lists the declared slots.
- The check exits 1; see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/docs/check-your-docs`.

#### Links (building-blocks/docs/links)

Link one doc to another so the link keeps working when the doc moves.

##### Link another doc

Write `{@link [provider:]kind:name}` in prose, list items, and table cells to link another doc. The CLI prints the command that opens it, so the link keeps working when the doc moves.

```javascript
{type: 'prose', text: 'Before you ship, read {@link generic:deploying}.'},
{type: 'list', style: 'unordered', items: ['All guides: {@link namespace:acme}.']},
{type: 'table', headers: ['Task', 'Guide'], rows: [['Ship', '{@link generic:deploying}']]},
```

Each link reads as a command. This link, `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/docs/extend-or-replace`, opens the next guide.

- The kind is `generic` for a topic or guide, `namespace` for a docs section, `command` or `function` for a CLI command or API function, `schema` or `enum` for a schema or a fixed set of values, `component` for a component, and `page` or `block` for a template.
- Name a component by its export name and a template by its id. Its link reads as the command that opens it, such as `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 component AcmeCarousel --package @acme/widgets`.
- Inside backticks or a code block, link syntax prints as written.

##### Link another package's docs

A link without a provider resolves against your own package. To link the CLI's docs, or another package's, start the target with that package's name, such as `@astryxdesign/cli:`.

```javascript
// Resolves: the CLI's doctor command
{type: 'prose', text: 'Check the app with {@link @astryxdesign/cli:command:doctor}.'},
// Does not resolve: looks for a doctor command in your package
{type: 'prose', text: 'Check the app with {@link command:doctor}.'},
```

- Name a CLI command the way you type it, spaces included, such as `@astryxdesign/cli:command:doctor integration docs`.
- In a topic that `extends` another package's topic, your sections still resolve against your package, so a link to the base topic's docs needs its provider.

##### Fix a link that names no doc

A link that names no doc prints as written, and `doctor integration docs` warns. The warning names a search that finds the right target.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration docs
```

```text
severity: [warn]
code:     invalid_doc_graph
message:  acme/deploying § check-before-you-ship: "command:doctor" names no doc. Find it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 search doctor --type doc`, then name it as `[<provider>:]<kind>:<name>`.
```

- The warning keeps exit code 0, so read the report before you ship; see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/docs/check-your-docs`.
- Published 0.6.4 and later read links. An older CLI, such as published 0.6.3, prints each one as written; see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/versioning`.

#### Extend or replace a topic (building-blocks/docs/extend-or-replace)

Take over a topic or guide, or merge sections into it.

##### Replace a topic

Set `replaces` to take over an existing topic, such as Core's `getting-started`. Readers who open the old name get your topic.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration add doc acme-getting-started --replaces getting-started
# The old name now opens your topic
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs getting-started
```

docs/acme-getting-started.doc.mjs:
```javascript
export default {
  type: 'generic',
  name: 'acme-getting-started',
  replaces: 'getting-started',
  title: 'Acme getting started',
  description: 'Install Acme widgets and render your first carousel.',
  sections: [/* ... */],
};
```

The docs list shows your topic in place of the old one. Because your topic has its own `name`, the old name keeps resolving to it, so links and agents that learned the old name still land on your topic.

##### Extend a topic

Set `extends` to merge sections into an existing topic instead of owning it. A section replaces the base section it matches, and a section that matches none is added at the end.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration add doc acme-theming --extends theme
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs theme --index
```

docs/acme-theming.doc.mjs:
```javascript
export default {
  type: 'generic',
  name: 'acme-theming',
  extends: 'theme',
  title: 'Acme theming',
  description: 'Theme an app that uses Acme widgets.',
  sections: [
    {id: 'quick-start', title: 'Quick Start', content: [/* replaces the base section */]},
    {id: 'use-the-ocean-theme', title: 'Use the ocean theme', content: [/* added at the end */]},
  ],
};
```

- Read the base topic's keys with `--index`, and give a section that replaces one that key as its `id`. A section that replaces one keeps its place. A section without an `id` matches only a base section with exactly its title, or one whose `id` is the key its title makes, so `Integration Themes` is added beside a base `Integration themes` that has no `id`.
- Set `before` or `after` to a base section's key to add a new section there instead of at the end. A key that names no section adds it at the end, and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration validate` lists a note. An older CLI rejects these fields, so declare an `@astryxdesign/cli` peer range that starts at the release that reads them; `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration verify` warns without it.
- The topic keeps the base's title and description, and readers open it by the base's name.
- Replace the `Overview` placeholder that `integration add` writes, or it is added to the base topic.
- Extend a topic to correct or add to it. A copy made with `replaces` stops getting the owner's fixes.

##### Replace or extend a CLI guide

A guide in the CLI's docs tree has a route rather than a topic name. Set `replaces` or `extends` to that route to change the guide for every app that installs your package: say what differs for your users on the page agents already read.

docs/acme-quick-start.doc.mjs:
```javascript
export default {
  type: 'generic',
  name: 'acme-quick-start',
  extends: 'authoring/quick-start',
  title: 'Acme quick start',
  description: 'What differs when you build integrations at Acme.',
  sections: [
    {id: 'use-the-acme-registry', title: 'Use the Acme registry', before: 'fill-in-package-json', content: [/* ... */]},
  ],
};
```

- Your doc stays a flat topic: do not give it a `placement`. Readers open the guide by its route, never by your `name`.
- With `replaces`, readers of the route get your doc, under your package. With `extends`, each section you add or replace names your package.
- A name that holds no topic or guide, such as a namespace, changes nothing; `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration validate` lists it as a note, with the guides below a namespace.

```bash
# Every guide route, by namespace
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring --depth all
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli --depth all
# The keys to place sections by
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/quick-start --index
```

##### Check overlaps with Core topics

A topic sets `replaces` or `extends`, never both, and a placed guide sets neither. A topic that uses a Core topic's name with neither is an accidental conflict: apps keep reading the Core topic.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration docs
```

```text
severity:     [info]
topic:        acme-getting-started
relationship: replaces
coreTopic:    getting-started
message:      Intentional override: "acme-getting-started" replaces the Core topic "getting-started".

severity:     [fail]
topic:        color
relationship: accidental
coreTopic:    color
message:      Accidental conflict: "color" is already a Core topic. Rename it, declare replaces: 'color' to take it over, or declare extends: 'color' to merge sections.
```

- An intentional overlap prints as `[info]`. An accidental one fails with exit code 1.
- A topic that sets both fails as `invalid_doc`, and so does a placed guide that sets either one.

##### In global mode

In global mode: a doc that extends or replaces a topic from a package installed for the computer applies in folders outside any project; inside a project, only those from packages the project installs apply. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/global-integrations`.

#### Short and findable (building-blocks/docs/short-and-findable)

Write short sections that people and agents find by search.

##### Keep each read short

Readers open one section at a time, so give each section one idea and keep it to about 30 lines. `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor` warns on any read over 32 KB.

- When a section needs a second idea, split it into two sections.
- Keep a topic to a few sections. When it grows past five, split it into more guides in your docs section.
- A topic with more than one section reads as its section list. Readers open one section by its key, or the whole topic with `--full`.

```bash
# The section list
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs acme/deploying
# One section
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs acme/deploying check-before-you-ship
# Everything
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs acme/deploying --full
```

##### Lead with the summary

A section's first prose block, or its first list item, is its summary in section lists and search results. Make it answer the section's question in one or two sentences.

- The summary is cut at about 240 characters.
- A code block first does not count: the summary comes from the next prose block.
- Open with the answer, not with background.

```text
build-before-you-ship  Build before you ship - Build the app, then upload the `dist` folder.
```

##### Make docs findable

In a topic with more than one section, search ranks a section whose title matches the query, or that names it in backticks, above words in body text. Title each section with the task a reader searches for.

- Name the task in the words a reader types, such as "Deploy to production". Avoid titles such as "Overview" or "Details".
- Write field names, file names, and error codes in backticks, such as `deployTarget`: in a topic with more than one section, search treats each one as a keyword.
- Other words in the summary and body match too, but rank below titles and identifiers. The summary shows under each hit, so make it answer the query.

##### Test with search

Test a doc the way a new reader finds it: search for the question, and check that the first hit answers it. Quote a query of more than one word.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 search "place a doc" --type doc
```

- This query returns the section of these guides that shows how to place a doc.
- Run the same search in an app that installs your package; see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/test-in-an-app`.

#### Check your docs (building-blocks/docs/check-your-docs)

Check the docs tree, links, overlaps, doc fields, read size, and CLI peer.

##### Run the docs check

Run `doctor integration docs` in your package to check the docs tree, every link, and overlaps with Core topics, and to list any passage two topics repeat. Pass a package name to check an installed package.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration docs
# In an app, check an installed package
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration docs @acme/astryx-widgets
```

```text
Checking integration docs: @acme/astryx-widgets@1.0.0

[ok] The docs tree and every link in these docs check out.

[ok] No doc topics overlap with Core.
[ok] No topic copies a passage from another.
[ok] No filler phrases or low-density topics.
```

Write each fact in one topic. When two of your topics, or one of yours and a Core topic, repeat 10 or more words of prose word for word, the check lists the pair as a `copied_passage` warning. It names the topic that keeps the text (a Core topic, or of your two the one the passage fits) and the line in the other where to put the link instead (`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/docs/links`). Code and examples are not compared, and a topic may carry the text of the Core topic it replaces. A run with fewer than 4 distinct content words (words other than function words such as "the", "in" or "it"), or one that three or more topics share (a series lead-in), is not listed. Each listed pair is also a warning (`copied_passage`): `doctor integration docs` still exits 0, and `integration check --strict` fails until you fix it.

Keep docs dense. The check lists, as a `doc_fluff` warning, each padding phrase in your prose, with its file line and what to write instead, and each topic of 80 or more prose words in which fewer than half the words carry content (words other than function words such as the, and, in), with its measured share and the floor of 0.5. `doctor integration docs` still exits 0, and `integration check --strict` fails until you cut it. Code, examples, and quoted text are not read. The phrases: `it's important to note`, `it is important to note`, `important to note that`, `it's worth noting`, `it is worth noting`, `worth noting that`, `it should be noted`, `please note`, `note that` (opening a sentence), `as mentioned above`, `as mentioned earlier`, `as mentioned before`, `as noted above`, `as you can see`, `needless to say`, `in order to`, `due to the fact that`, `for the purpose of`, `at this point in time`, `in other words`, `basically`, `essentially`, `obviously`.

Point at another doc with a link, never by writing `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs <name>` in prose: `{@link generic:<name>}` for one of your package's topics, or `{@link @astryxdesign/cli:generic:<name>}` for a Core doc (`namespace:` for a Core namespace). The CLI prints the link as the command that opens the doc, and doctor checks that the doc exists. The check lists each written pointer to a doc that exists as a `stray_doc_pointer` warning, with the link to write instead. A command with more words, or one in a code block, is a walkthrough and is not listed.

Its arguments and exit codes are in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/doctor-integration-docs`.

##### Know what fails the check

A doc that does not load, an accidental Core overlap, a `reference` block that names no doc, or a failed namespace or placement fails the check with exit code 1. A link that names no doc only warns, and the exit code stays 0.

Problem                                                                  | Reported as                      | Exit code
------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ---------
A doc that does not load, such as an unknown section field or block type | `[fail]` `invalid_doc`           | 1        
A topic with a Core topic's name and no `replaces` or `extends`          | `[fail]` `accidental`            | 1        
A placement that fails, which hides the doc                              | `[fail]` `invalid_doc_graph`     | 1        
A `reference` block whose target names no doc                            | `[fail]` `invalid_doc_reference` | 1        
A link that names no doc                                                 | `[warn]` `invalid_doc_graph`     | 0        
A topic that sets `replaces` or `extends`                                | `[info]` `replaces` or `extends` | 0        

Read the warnings before you publish. With `--json`, they are in `data.issues`, with `severity: "warning"`.

##### Check each doc against its type

`doctor integration validate` reads every doc your package ships against the type `@astryxdesign/cli/authoring` publishes for its kind, the way `tsc` would: a `hidden` doc and a second doc for one name too. Test fixtures under `__tests__` in the components or docs root, which those readers skip, are counted, not checked. It reports a field the type does not have (`unknown_field`), a missing required field (`missing_field`), and a value outside the field's type (`wrong_type`).

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration validate
```

```text
Checking 1 doc(s) against the authoring types (TypeScript 6.0.3)

severity: [warn]
doc:      components/AcmeCarousel.doc.mjs
line:     7
export:   default
type:     ComponentDoc
field:    summary
problem:  unknown_field
message:  Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'summary' does not exist in type 'SingleComponentDoc'.
fix:      Remove `summary`: SingleComponentDoc has no field `summary`.
```

- The folder decides the type: `ComponentDoc` in your components root, `IntegrationTemplateDoc` in your templates root, `ThemeDoc` in your themes root, and in your docs root the type the doc's `type` names. Keep the `@type` comment above each doc's export too, so your editor shows the same problems as you type.
- Every finding is a warning, so the exit code stays 0. With `--json`, they are in `data.docTypes.findings`.
- It uses the `typescript` your package installs. Where `typescript` is missing or has no JavaScript compiler API, as TypeScript 7 does, it uses `@typescript/typescript6`, the TypeScript 6 API package, if your package installs it. Without either, it prints `[skip] Docs not type-checked` and the reason.
- Every field of every doc type is in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/field-reference`.

##### Check read size

`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor` also measures every read and warns on one over 32 KB. Run it in your package or in an app that installs it; `doctor integration docs` does not check size.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor
```

```text
id:      docs-progressive-disclosure
status:  [warn]
label:   Documentation navigation and size
message: acme/deploying build-before-you-ship: 46 KB, over the 32 KB one read may return
```

Split a section over the limit into smaller ones, each with its own key. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/doctor`.

##### Check the CLI peer

`integration verify` fails a package that ships a docs section, a placed guide, or a doc section with an `id` without an `@astryxdesign/cli` peer of `>=0.6.4`. It does not run the docs check, so run both.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration verify
```

```text
- [fail] The package ships a namespace doc or a placed guide but declares no @astryxdesign/cli peer. A stable CLI before 0.6.4 does not read the docs tree, and can hide every doc topic the package ships. Declare "@astryxdesign/cli": ">=0.6.4" in peerDependencies (optional in peerDependenciesMeta, if the CLI is not required).
```

- `integration add doc --parent` writes the peer for you.
- `integration verify` passes a hidden guide and an accidental Core overlap; only `doctor integration docs` catches them.
- Everything else it checks is in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/integration-verify` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/checks`.

### Codemods (building-blocks/codemods)

Ship codemods that `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 upgrade` runs to migrate app code, and know which of them an app runs.

#### Add a codemod

`integration add codemod` writes a codemod into a folder named after a version. Apps run it with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 upgrade` to migrate their code.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration add codemod rename-delay --to 0.7.0
```

```text
codemods/
  0.7.0/
    rename-delay.mjs         # the codemod
    rename-delay.test.mjs    # skipped: a test file
    __tests__/               # skipped: a test folder
```

The first add declares `codemods: './codemods'` in `astryx.integration.mjs`. The codemod's id is its path inside the version folder, without the extension: `rename-delay`. An id must be unique across all version folders in the package.

The loader skips `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, and `*.fixture.*` files and everything under `__tests__/` or `__fixtures__/`, so tests can sit beside the codemod. The folder name decides when an app runs the codemod; see "Choose when a codemod runs".

#### Write the transform

A codemod default-exports a plain object with a `type`, a `title`, and a `transform` function. `transform` returns the new source, or `null` to leave the file as it is.

```js
// codemods/0.7.0/rename-delay.mjs
/** @type {import('@astryxdesign/cli/authoring').AstryxCodemod} */
export default {
  type: 'code',
  title: 'Rename AcmeCarousel delay to interval',
  description: 'Renames the delay prop on AcmeCarousel.',
  fileExtensions: ['.tsx', '.jsx'],
  transform(file, api) {
    const j = api.jscodeshift;
    const root = j(file.source);
    const props = root
      .find(j.JSXOpeningElement, {name: {name: 'AcmeCarousel'}})
      .find(j.JSXAttribute, {name: {name: 'delay'}});
    if (props.size() === 0) return null;
    props.forEach(path => {
      path.node.name.name = 'interval';
    });
    return root.toSource();
  },
};
```

`type: 'code'` rewrites the app's source files that match `fileExtensions`. `type: 'config'` rewrites the app's `astryx.config` file instead, and runs before code codemods. `title` shows in the upgrade output, and `api.jscodeshift` is a jscodeshift instance for the file. Every field is in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring codemod`.

#### Choose when a codemod runs

Two rules decide whether an app's `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 upgrade` runs your codemods: the app's Core versions, and whether the app names your package.

1. Version folders are matched against the app's `@astryxdesign/core` versions, not your package's version. `upgrade --from <version>` runs each folder above `--from`, up to and including the Core version installed in the app. With Core 0.7.0 installed, `--from 0.6.3` runs `0.7.0/`, and `--from 0.7.0` runs nothing. A folder named after your own release, such as `1.0.0/`, waits until the app has Core 1.0.0.
2. `upgrade` runs your codemods only when the app lists your package in `integrations` in its `astryx.config`, or passes `--integration @acme/astryx-widgets`. Having your package installed is not enough: the run then skips your codemods with no warning.

#### Run codemods in an app

An app previews codemods with `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 upgrade` and writes the changes with `--apply`. Without `--apply`, nothing on disk changes.

```bash
# Preview each codemod and the files it would change
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 upgrade --from 0.6.3 --integration @acme/astryx-widgets
# Write the changes
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 upgrade --from 0.6.3 --integration @acme/astryx-widgets --apply
```

```text
Integrations: @acme/astryx-widgets
<n> codemods to run (dry run)
Applying integration codemods...
  Rename AcmeCarousel delay to interval (v0.7.0, @acme/astryx-widgets)
!     ~ src/Hero.tsx (would change)
```

`<n>` counts Core's codemods for the same versions too: they run first and print above `Integrations:`. To run only yours, as when you test it, add `--codemod rename-delay`.

`--from` is the Core version the app had before it upgraded. The run scans `./src` unless the app passes `--path`, and it never writes a file the app marks as generated, vendored, or ignored; see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/upgrade`. `upgrade --list` shows only Core codemods.

An integration manifest has no `hooks` field. Commands that run after codemods, such as a formatter, are the app's to set, in `hooks.postCodemod` in its `astryx.config`.

#### In global mode

In global mode: inside an app, `upgrade` runs with the release equal to the app's Core, whichever copy of the CLI the user starts, and only the codemods of integrations the app installs run. Outside a project, `upgrade` lists codemods and migrates nothing. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/upgrade`.

### Configuration (building-blocks/configuration)

Set how your integration behaves in an app: agent guidance, the command your users run, debug and gap reports, and more as it grows.

In global mode: installed for the computer, beside the global CLI, your package's manifest is read as it is in a project and applies in folders outside any project; peer ranges are checked against the global CLI's release. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/global-integrations`.

Beyond the things you ship, an integration can set how it behaves in an app: the guidance it gives the AI agents working there, the command its users run the CLI with, and the record it keeps of each CLI run. Open one below to set it up.

#### Agent guidance (building-blocks/configuration/agent-guidance)

Add a few lines of guidance that apps put in front of the AI agents working in their code.

##### Add a line of guidance

`integration add agent-doc` adds one line for AI agents that work in apps using your package. Apps show it in their agent file, such as `AGENTS.md`.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration add agent-doc 'Use AcmeCarousel for rotating content.'
```

The line lands in `agentDocs.append` in your manifest:

```js
// astryx.integration.mjs
export default {
  components: './components',
  agentDocs: {
    append: ['Use AcmeCarousel for rotating content.'],
  },
};
```

Adding the same line again changes nothing. To reword or remove a line, edit `agentDocs.append` by hand.

##### Keep within the limits

Every line costs space in each app's agent file, so the CLI keeps guidance short and few. Put detail in your docs instead.

Limit                                   | What happens past it                                                    
--------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------
8 lines per package                     | `integration add` fails: `append may contain at most 8 lines`.          
240 characters per line                 | `integration add` fails: `must contain at most 240 Unicode code points`.
32 lines per app, from all its packages | `init` writes no agent block and prints `Could not install agent docs.` 

A line is one line of plain text. Line breaks, control characters, spaces at either end, and managed-block markers such as `<!-- ASTRYX:START -->` are rejected.

Start a command in a line with the word astryx alone, with no runner in front, as in: Run astryx doctor before finishing. The block names the command the app runs once, at its top, for every command below it, so your line works in every app. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/configuration/cli-command`.

##### See what agents read

An app's `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init` writes your lines at the end of its managed agent block, each labeled with your package name. The CLI owns the heading, the labels, and the markers.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init --features agents
```

```text
INTEGRATIONS:
- `@acme/astryx-widgets`: Use AcmeCarousel for rotating content.
<!-- ASTRYX:END -->
```

The block collects lines from every integration the app has installed, with or without an `astryx.config` entry.

##### Refresh the block in an app

The block changes only when the app runs `init`, or `upgrade --from <version> --apply`. After an app installs a version of your package with new lines, it runs one of them.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init --features agents
# Or: --from takes the Core version the app had before
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 upgrade --from <version> --apply
```

```text
[ok] Agent docs refreshed -> AGENTS.md
```

`upgrade --apply` prints that line; `init` prints `[ok] AI agent docs installed -> AGENTS.md`. Without `--apply`, `upgrade` only reports `Agent docs differ from the installed Astryx and integration configuration.` It refreshes the block even when Core did not change. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/upgrade`.

##### In global mode

In global mode: the agent guide the CLI keeps for the computer carries no integration's guidance, because it serves every folder; your guidance reaches agents through the agent docs `init` writes in an app that installs your package. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/computer-agent-guide`.

#### CLI command (building-blocks/configuration/cli-command)

Name the command your users run the CLI with, so every command the CLI prints in their apps starts with it.

##### When to set it

The CLI ends most answers with the next command to run: a hint, an error fix, a Doctor fix, or a doc example. By default each one starts with a command that reaches the release that answered: what the app's package manager runs, such as `pnpm exec astryx` or `yarn astryx`, when the app's own CLI answered, and otherwise the CLI package pinned to that release, such as `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.2`.

Set `cliCommand` only when your users run the CLI some other way, such as a wrapper your company ships that runs it with your package loaded. Otherwise the commands the CLI prints send them, and their agents, to a CLI that answers without your package. Most packages leave it out.

##### Set it

Add `cliCommand` to `astryx.integration.mjs`: the command, without a subcommand.

```js
// astryx.integration.mjs
export default {
  components: './components',
  cliCommand: 'acme astryx',
};
```

In an app that installs your package, the CLI then prints every command with it:

```text
Error: Theme "ocean" is not added. Run `acme astryx theme add ocean` first.
```

That covers hints, errors, suggestions, Doctor fixes, `--help`, the setup reminder, the agent block `init` writes, and doc text. `--json` output keeps every command without a runner, as in `"command": "astryx theme add ocean"`, so a script reads the same fields in every app.

##### How the CLI picks the command

1. The `cliCommand` of the packages the app loads, when they name one command.
2. The command a host tool names when it runs the CLI for the app. Nothing in a plain project names one.
3. A command that reaches the release that answered: what the app's package manager runs when the app's own CLI answered, such as `pnpm exec astryx` or `yarn astryx`; `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12` outside a project when the CLI installed for the computer answered; otherwise the CLI package pinned to that release, such as `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.2` (see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/who-answers`).

Two packages that set the same command agree, and the CLI uses it.

##### When two packages disagree

If two packages an app loads set different commands, the CLI uses neither: it prints commands with what the app's package manager runs, even when a host tool named a command. `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor` warns in its `cli-command` check and names both packages:

```text
status:  [warn]
label:   CLI command
message: Loaded integrations declare different CLI commands: @acme/astryx-widgets (`acme astryx`), @other/kit (`other astryx`). Neither is used, so printed commands start with `pnpm exec astryx`.
```

The app fixes it by removing the package that does not belong, or the packages agree on one command.

##### Check it

An invalid value is ignored, and the rest of your manifest still loads. `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration validate` reports it as `invalid_cli_command`. A valid `cliCommand` is one line of plain text without spaces at either end, at most 120 characters.

In an app that installs your package, `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor` passes its `cli-command` check and names your package as the one that set the command. A CLI released before this field reports `cliCommand` as an unknown key and prints the package manager's command.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration validate
# In an app that installs the package
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor
```

##### In global mode

In global mode: outside a project, the `cliCommand` of integrations installed for the computer applies; when none is declared, commands start with the plain command of the CLI installed for the computer. Inside a project, only the project's integrations count, so a `cliCommand` from a package installed for the computer never changes the project's printed commands. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/global-integrations`.

#### Debug and gap reports (building-blocks/configuration/debug-and-gap-reports)

Receive a record of each CLI run in apps that use your package, and handle the gap reports they send about it.

##### Record runs with debug

Export a `debug` function from `astryx.integration.mjs`; the CLI calls it once per command run in an app loading your package.

```js
// astryx.integration.mjs
import {appendFileSync} from 'node:fs';

/** @param {import('@astryxdesign/cli/authoring').DebugEvent} event */
export function debug(event) {
  if (event.outcome !== 'ok') {
    appendFileSync('acme-failed-runs.ndjson', JSON.stringify(event) + '\n');
  }
}

export default {
  components: './components',
};
```

The event is a `DebugEvent` with `command`, `outcome`, `exitCode`, `durationMs`, `error`, and more, its values scrubbed (`redacted: true`). Every field is in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring debug-event`.

Keep the function synchronous: the CLI calls it as the process exits and never waits for a promise. The app's own `debug` handler runs first, then yours. A handler that throws is skipped, and the command's output and exit code stay the same.

An app records every command only when its `astryx.config` names `integrations` or `debug`, as listing your package does. Otherwise your handler runs only for commands loading the app's project, such as `component` and `docs`, never for `--version` or a mistyped command. In an app whose config names neither word, those commands also print a stderr warning.

`debug` is a named export, not a manifest field, so an older CLI ignores it and loads the rest of your manifest.

##### Turn off debug in an app

An app can refuse every integration's `debug` handler and keep its own. It sets `inheritDebug` in its package.json:

```json
{"astryx": {"inheritDebug": false}}
```

Your handler then no longer runs in that app.

##### Handle gap reports

Export a `gapReport` handler, and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 gap-report` in an app sends it each gap report, such as a missing component or variant. The handler files the report and returns a receipt.

```js
/** @type {import('@astryxdesign/cli/authoring').GapReportHandler} */
export const gapReport = {
  audience: 'public',
  async handle(report, {signal}) {
    if (report.target.package !== '@acme/astryx-widgets') return {status: 'skipped'};
    const body = JSON.stringify(report);
    const response = await fetch('https://tracker.example.com/issues', {method: 'POST', body, signal});
    const {url} = await response.json();
    return {status: 'filed', url};
  },
};
```

Every handler in the app gets every report, so check `report.target.package` and skip reports about other packages.

Every field is in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring gap-report-handler`.

The CLI waits 30 seconds, then aborts `signal`. A throw, a timeout, or an invalid receipt fails your delivery, and the command exits 1; the other handlers still run. Like `debug`, `gapReport` is a named export that older CLIs ignore.

##### Ask before filing in public

Set `audience: 'public'` when your handler writes somewhere the public can read. The CLI runs it only when the caller passes `--confirm-public`; an `'internal'` handler always runs.

```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 gap-report AcmeCarousel --category missing_variant --reason 'Need a vertical layout'
```

```text
handlerType: integration
handler:     @acme/astryx-widgets
audience:    public
status:      consent_required
message:     Rerun with --confirm-public to file this report.
```

With `--confirm-public`, the same delivery reads `status: filed` and shows your `url`. The report goes to the package named by `--package`, else the package that owns the component, else Core.

##### Fall back to issuesUrl

With no `gapReport` handler in the app, the CLI routes the report to the target package's manifest `issuesUrl`.

- A GitHub issues URL, such as `https://github.com/acme/widgets/issues`, gets an issue filed with the GitHub CLI, `gh`, once the caller passes `--confirm-public`.
- Any other URL comes back as a `routed_only` receipt for the caller to open.
- With no `issuesUrl`, the command fails: `Package "@acme/astryx-widgets" provides neither a report handler nor an issues URL.`

One handler anywhere in the app, from the app or from any package, turns the fallback off for every report. So does a listed package that fails to load: the CLI cannot tell whether it has a handler, so the report fails for that package instead of going to another tracker. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/gap-report`.

##### Let the person choose where a report goes

When an app loads packages naming their own `issuesUrl`, a report can go to the default (the handlers, or the fallback above) or to one of those packages. `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 gap-report --list-categories` and the receipt of a report filed without `--to` list every destination, with a line telling the agent to ask the person.

- An agent asks the person where to file. It never picks a package destination on its own.
- `--to <package>` carries the person's choice: the report goes only to that package's `issuesUrl`, under the same `--confirm-public` rule, and no handler runs.
- Without a choice, leave out `--to`; the report goes to the default.
- A `--to` that names no destination fails before anything is sent and lists the destinations.

##### In global mode

In global mode: when users install your package for their computer, beside the global CLI, its `debug` function receives runs in folders outside any project too; inside a project, only if the project installs it. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global` and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/global-integrations`.

## Make your integration work globally (global-integrations)

People can install your integration next to their global Astryx install, where it works in every folder outside a project; inside a project, only the project's own integrations work. A checklist, with the exact commands to try it.

### First: your peer ranges must include the global CLI's version

Your `@astryxdesign/core` (and, if you use it, `@astryxdesign/cli`) `peerDependencies` ranges must include the version of the CLI installed globally. If they do not, Astryx skips your package outside projects, and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor` warns and names the range.

Inside a project that does not install your package, `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 discover` offers it, with the command that adds it to that project, once your peer range admits the project's release.

### Where your integration works

- Installed in an app: it works in that app, as always, whichever `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12` the person runs, because the app's version of Astryx answers there.
- Installed next to the global install (`npm install -g @astryxdesign/cli your-package`), or in the same folder as the CLI by a tool that installs them together: it works in every folder outside a project. People and agents there see its components, templates, docs, themes, codemods, and discover source.
- Installed only globally, inside an app that does not install it: it adds nothing there. When it supports the app's version and loads, `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 discover` lists it as one the app could add, with the app's install command.
- Installed both ways: the app's copy is the one used in that app. In your own package folder, your working copy is used.

Astryx loads a global integration with the same loader and checks as an app's, so nothing extra goes in your manifest.

### Checklist

- Declare the `@astryxdesign/core` (and, if you use it, `@astryxdesign/cli`) `peerDependencies` range your package really supports. Outside a project, Astryx skips your package when that range leaves out the global version, and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor` says why: too narrow, and global users lose it after an upgrade; too wide, and it loads against a Core it may not build with.
- Keep imports in your docs and templates to packages an app installs with yours, since outside a project there is no app to check them against.
- If you set `cliCommand`, know that outside a project it starts every command Astryx prints, and that two global integrations naming different commands cancel out, falling back to `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12` (`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/configuration/cli-command`). Inside an app, only the app's integrations count.
- Try it globally before you publish, with the steps below.

### Try it globally

Pack your package, install it next to a global CLI, and look at it from an empty folder:

```bash
npm pack  # only with npm: the tarball the registry receives
npm install -g @astryxdesign/cli ./your-package-1.0.0.tgz
mkdir -p /tmp/try-global && cd /tmp/try-global
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 discover
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor
```

- `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 discover` lists your package as installed, with what it adds.
- `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs` lists your topics, and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 search <one of your component names>` finds them.
- `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor`'s `computer-integrations` check lists your package as used, with no warning.
- In an app that does not install it, `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 discover` lists it as one the app could add, with the app's install command, and none of its components or docs show up.

Remove it again with `npm uninstall -g your-package`.

### More on global mode

Every integration runs `integration check --strict` in its own build, so every build keeps your docs, types, and links in sync; this is required, not optional. The strict check fails on every copied passage the docs check lists (`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/docs/check-your-docs`). Run `integration verify` before you publish. Install devDependencies first, because the components check needs Core, and `tsc --noEmit` needs `typescript` and a `tsconfig.json`. In package.json:

```json
"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit && astryx integration check --strict"
```

- `integration check` runs `validate`, `components`, `templates`, and `docs` in that order, prints each result, then a summary, and exits 1 when any of them would.
- `--strict` also exits 1 on any warning and on any check that did not run. Without it, warnings keep exit code 0: use that while you fix the warnings a package already has.
- Its exit codes and JSON are a contract for your build: a new check, or a new failure code, joins only in a minor release that names it in the release notes. A patch can still ship a Core component, template, or CLI topic whose name conflicts with one of yours.
- `integration verify` runs `validate` but none of the other three: a Core name clash, a `replaces` that names no Core template, a topic that takes a Core name, or a hidden guide still passes it. Run both before you publish: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration check --strict && astryx integration verify`.
- Bare `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor` in the package also warns about a doc section over 32 KB, which no check above measures.

#### Verify the packed package

`integration verify` packs your package with npm, unpacks it into a temporary app, and checks that the app sees everything your source has. It publishes nothing and leaves no `.tgz` file or temporary folder behind.

1. It runs `npm pack` (only with npm: the tarball the registry receives) the way `npm publish` (only with npm: npm is the client the registry publishes from) would, including your `prepack` script.
2. It checks that every contribution file is in the `.tgz` file. A root missing from `files` fails with `Add "templates" to "files" in package.json.`
3. It lists the components, templates, themes, docs, and codemods the temporary app sees, and compares them with your source.
4. It resolves each component's `import`, and each template's public import, the way Node does, and checks that the module exports the component under the name its doc documents, or a default export for a template. A type-only export does not count.
5. For each theme, it rebuilds the source, compares the built module and production CSS with the authored outputs, and proves the module, CSS, and optional font CSS exports resolve from the packed package.
6. It fails a package that needs an `@astryxdesign/cli` peer and lacks it: `>=0.6.6` for a template that sets `keywords`, and `>=0.6.4` for a template that sets `replaces`, a docs section, a placed guide, a doc section with an `id`, or a theme.

`integration pack --check`, the name this check had before published 0.6.5, still runs it and prints a note; it will be removed in a later release. The options and exit codes are in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/integration-verify`.

### Versioning (ship/versioning)

Version your package, declare its peers, and keep apps on older CLIs working.

#### Pick a version

Version your package with semver: a major version for a breaking change, a minor version for a new feature, and a patch for a fix.

```bash
# 1.0.0 -> 2.0.0: a breaking change
npm version major  # only with npm: npm, which every Node install carries, sets the version
# 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0: a new feature
npm version minor  # only with npm: npm, which every Node install carries, sets the version
# 1.0.0 -> 1.0.1: a fix
npm version patch  # only with npm: npm, which every Node install carries, sets the version
```

- Before 1.0.0, npm treats each minor version as breaking: an app that asks for `^0.6.0` never gets `0.7.0`. Bump the minor version for a breaking change, and the patch for anything else.
- Ship a codemod with each breaking change so apps can migrate; see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/codemods`.

#### Know what breaks apps

A breaking change stops code, commands, or links that worked in an app from working after the upgrade. For an integration, these names are part of its API.

You change or remove                            | What stops working in the app                                        
----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------
A component name, such as `AcmeCarousel`        | Imports, and `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 component AcmeCarousel`   
A template id, such as `acme-dashboard`         | `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 template acme-dashboard`               
A theme slug, such as `ocean`                   | `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 theme add ocean`                       
A topic name or route, such as `acme/deploying` | Reads of the old name, and links to it from other docs               
A component's `import` path                     | Imports written from the old path                                    
An `exports` entry                              | Imports of that path, which fail with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`
A prop                                          | Code that passes it                                                  

List each breaking change in your release notes, with the codemod that migrates it. Any changelog tool works. If `package.json` has a `files` allowlist, add `CHANGELOG.md` to it so npm packs it.

#### Declare peer ranges

Declare the Astryx packages that your code imports as peer dependencies, in `peerDependencies`, so the app installs one copy of each. Keep each range as wide as your tests prove.

Peer                    | Declare it when                                                                                                                                                  | Range                                                                                                                                                       
----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
`@astryxdesign/core`    | Your code imports Core, as a theme does with `@astryxdesign/core/theme`                                                                                          | The Core versions you test, such as `^0.6.0`                                                                                                                
`@astryxdesign/theme-*` | Your code imports that theme package                                                                                                                             | The versions you test                                                                                                                                       
`@astryxdesign/cli`     | You ship a docs section, a placed guide, a template that sets `replaces` or `keywords`, a component that sets `replaces`, a doc section with an `id`, or a theme | `>=0.6.6` when you ship a template that sets `keywords`, `>=0.6.7` when a component sets `replaces`, otherwise `>=0.6.4`. Optional in `peerDependenciesMeta`

```json
{
  "peerDependencies": {
    "@astryxdesign/core": "^0.6.0",
    "@astryxdesign/cli": ">=0.6.4"
  },
  "peerDependenciesMeta": {
    "@astryxdesign/cli": {"optional": true}
  }
}
```

`integration verify` fails a package that needs the CLI peer and lacks it, or whose range admits a stable CLI too old for what it ships. `integration add doc --parent` and `integration add theme` write the peer for you.

When the CLI is outside that range, `doctor integration validate` and `integration check` list a `cli_peer_version` note naming your package. A note fails nothing, `--strict` included, and `integration verify` does not report it. Below the range the note gives the commands that install a newer Core and CLI together, as dev dependencies in your own package folder, and then run `upgrade --apply`. Above it, in an app the note asks for a release of your package that supports that CLI, and in your own package folder it asks you to test your package with that CLI and widen the range.

#### Support older CLIs

An app may run an older CLI than the one you build with. A CLI reads what it knows and skips the rest, but some newer files make an older CLI hide your docs.

- An unknown field in `astryx.integration.mjs` is ignored with an `unknown_manifest_key` warning, and the rest of the manifest still loads.
- A named export that the CLI does not know is ignored with no warning, so `debug` and `gapReport` are safe to add.
- Published 0.6.3 and earlier print each `{@link ...}` as written.
- Published 0.6.3 and earlier reject a template that sets `replaces` or `keywords`, drop that template, and hide every doc topic your package ships. Published 0.6.4 and 0.6.5 still drop a template that sets `keywords`.
- Published 0.6.3 and earlier cannot read a docs section, a section `id`, or a theme folder that `integration add theme` writes. They can then hide every doc topic your package ships.
- Published 0.6.2 and 0.6.3 still load your components, but published 0.6.0 and 0.6.1 cannot read the component docs that `integration add component` writes: `component AcmeCarousel` fails there.
- An app on an older CLI lists a component whose doc names another export of its file under the file name, and lists no family members, so `component AcmeCarousel` fails there.

`integration verify` requires the CLI peer for a docs section, a placed guide, a template `replaces` or `keywords`, a doc section with an `id`, and a theme. A CLI too old for one of them cannot read it, and when it hides your topics, `docs` gives no warning.

#### Name codemod folders after Core versions

Name each codemod folder after the Core version whose upgrade should run it, not after your package's version. Which folders an app runs, and when, is in "Choose when a codemod runs" in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/codemods`.

npm publish --dry-run --access public  # only with npm: publishing goes through npm, which every Node install carries

+ @acme/astryx-widgets@1.0.0

With no `files` list, npm packs every file your ignore files do not exclude, including an old `.tgz` file or an `.env` file. List what ships instead.

npm pack --dry-run  # only with npm: builds the tarball npm publishes
```

- List only the roots you ship, and always `astryx.integration.mjs`. npm adds package.json, and a README and LICENSE when you have them.
- Each later `integration add` appends its root to the list.
- `integration verify` fails when a root is missing from the list, and names the root to add to `files` (the message is in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/help/troubleshooting`).

A scoped package is private by default, so publish it with `--access public`. Without `--tag`, npm tags the release `latest`, which is what `npm install @acme/astryx-widgets` installs.

```bash

npm publish --access public  # only with npm: publishing goes through npm, which every Node install carries

# Or set the access once in package.json
npm pkg set publishConfig.access=public  # only with npm: Yarn has no pkg command

To let apps try a release first, publish it under `next`, then point `latest` at it once ready.

```bash

npm publish --tag next  # only with npm: publishing goes through npm, which every Node install carries

# Make that version the default
npm dist-tag add @acme/astryx-widgets@1.1.0 latest  # only with npm: dist-tags are set with npm, which every Node install carries
npm dist-tag ls @acme/astryx-widgets  # only with npm: dist-tags are set with npm, which every Node install carries
```

### Upgrading (ship/upgrading)

Update your package for each Astryx release, and help apps upgrade with it.

#### Update for a new Astryx release

When Astryx ships a release, bump your devDependencies, rerun the checks, widen your peer ranges, and ship a codemod for each change that breaks apps.

```bash
# 1. Build and test against the new release
npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli@latest @astryxdesign/core@latest
# 2. Rerun the checks
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration validate
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 doctor integration docs
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration verify
# 3. Admit the new Core once the checks pass
npm pkg set 'peerDependencies.@astryxdesign/core=^0.6.0 || ^0.7.0'  # only with npm: edits package.json
# 4. Migrate apps across a change that breaks them
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration add codemod rename-delay --to 0.7.0
```

- Run every check in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/checks`, not only the ones shown.
- Codemod folders are named for Core versions: `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/building-blocks/codemods`.
- Release the result as a new version of your package; see `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs authoring/ship/publishing`.

#### Upgrade an app

After an app installs a new Core, `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 upgrade` runs the codemods for the versions it crossed. It is a dry run by default; `--apply` writes the changes.

```bash
# Preview what would change; nothing is written
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 upgrade --from 0.6.3 --integration @acme/astryx-widgets
# Write the changes
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 upgrade --from 0.6.3 --integration @acme/astryx-widgets --apply
```

```text
Integrations: @acme/astryx-widgets
<n> codemods to run
Applying integration codemods...
  Rename AcmeCarousel delay to interval (v0.7.0, @acme/astryx-widgets)
[ok]     [ok] src/Hero.tsx
```

- `--from` is the `@astryxdesign/core` version the app had before, and the target is the installed Core.
- `--integration` names your package. Without it, or an `integrations` entry in `astryx.config`, the upgrade skips your codemods, even when the app has your package installed.
- `<n>` includes Core's codemods for the same versions, which run first.
- Put this command in your release notes.

#### Know which files upgrades skip

Upgrades never write files that the app marks as generated, vendored, or ignored. When such a file still needs a codemod change, the upgrade stops with `ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED` and exit code 1.

- Generated: an `@generated` comment at the top of the file, or `linguist-generated` in `.gitattributes`.
- Vendored: `linguist-vendored` in `.gitattributes`.
- Ignored: a match in `.gitignore` or `.hgignore`.

```text
!     ! src/gen/Gen.tsx - protected by @generated in the leading comment block
ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED: 1 protected file still requires a codemod change:
  src/gen/Gen.tsx — @generated in the leading comment block
Upgrade incomplete: protected changes remain
```

The upgrade still writes every other file. Its options and exit codes are in `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/upgrade`.
